limitations: Each formal run selects one minimum-global-ID sample per class: 1000 total, 800 training classes and 200 heldout classes; not the original full 5000 per bank.
Only one sample per heldout class gives low power and noisy feature means. The same banks/splits were used before; this is retrospective.
Large finite endpoint remainder and cancellation do not identify a local guidance error or justify subtracting the remainder.
Empirical squared feature-mean errors omit covariance and other distribution structure; they and non-image linear counterfactuals are not FID or generation quality.
The raw Taylor integral requires twice differentiability along the segment; clamp has nonsmooth boundaries and is audited separately.
FP32 JVP at promoted endpoints is not the derivative of the production BF16 numerical mapping.
No candidate guidance, new sampled trajectory, new FID, or cost-matched quality claim. Full-5k expansion is not decided or authorized by this archive.

Train and heldout empirical mean-error directions differ: the linear counterfactual worsens raw unwhitened train mean error in both seeds but improves the heldout metric. This does not support a global linear-beneficial/nonlinear-harmful conclusion.
The 768-coordinate squared sample-mean error with only 200 heldout samples has finite-sample bias/variance; no bias correction or generation-quality interpretation is claimed.
